readings_ruling: DECISIVE. None of the three readings is load-bearing for a marked label, so the five marks stand without a DEC row. (2) |log|: in the printed order it is the printed value log (A', B', B, A) >= 0 (projMeasure_eq_log). For the other order it is the measure of the same unordered segment (projMeasure_swap, projMeasure_reverse). In Déf. 2 the majorising segment (A, B) is existential and can be named either way round (IsProjSegment Sg A B -> IsProjSegment Sg B A, audit probe), so every reading that agrees on the printed order gives the same IsMajoreSeg. (3) l_V as a function of the segment is the paper's own usage, not a choice: a segment is a part with endpoints (Ch. 1 Déf. 14, ch1 l.410-415); Déf. 3 says « d'un segment (M, N) »; 5° (l.245) says « fonction semi-continue supérieurement du segment »; 7° says « (M, N) un segment de V dont la pseudo-longueur »; Déf. 6 (l.411-415) says « au moins un segment fermé d'extrémités M, N ». The pair forms (Prop. 2, 6°) concern the interior of a convex body, where the segment is unique. Props 4-7 use majorised segments, never l_V of a pair. (1) has two cases. (1a) A' = A with B' != A, or B' = B with A' != B: the printed formula (pr/qr)(qs/ps) has a zero denominator, so its value is infinite and ⊤ = log ∞ is the printed value extended. Any reading in which a non-real measure is not < k gives the same Déf. 2. (1b) Coincident points: A' = B' at an endpoint (0/0) and A = B (four equal points). Here the paper defines no cross-ratio, and Déf. 1's « supérieure ou égale à l'unité » presupposes one, so ⊤ there is a convention outside the printed domain. For n >= 1 it changes nothing (audit probe: IsMajoreSeg n k {M} M M <-> 0 < k, the same under the alternative 'a point has measure 0', because M is interior to some segment of a chart). It bites only at n = 0, where every segment is a point whose only majorising candidate is itself (A = B). There the Lean follows the literal text: « mesure ... < k » with no measure is not satisfied. The alternative value 0 would add something the paper does not print. Hence the n = 0 consequence is reported correctly as a finding against 1°, not a reading in Déf. 2-4. Its wording needs care (finding 1). If the author nevertheless rules the coincident-point case a reading, the labels that move are Déf. 2, 3 and 4, and only in dimension 0. Déf. 1 does not move. This is the opposite of the REPORT's fallback (finding 2).

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d1_mesure_projective
labels.notes: Transcription l.262-268 checked against the scan, p. 249 (PDF p. 22): identical. IsCrossRatio A' B' B A r asks for independent representatives a of A and b of B, with a + b in F(A'), a + r b in F(B'), r > 0. So it holds only for A', B' in the open segment )A, B( with B != ±A, and it is functional (IsCrossRatio.unique). It is odds(B')/odds(A'). isCrossRatio_affine identifies it with crossRatio p q r s = (pr/qr)(qs/ps) on any line p0 + t d of E. Checked by hand: odds(t) = (t - s)/(r - t), and the ratio of the two odds is the formula. That is Benzécri's convention of p. 250, with the [sic] read. The 300 dpi crop of PDF p. 23 prints « af' × bf / (af × ff') ». p. 251 (« af'/bf' est supérieur à l'unité, en sorte que le quotient bf/af est inférieur à K ») confirms the reading af × bf', so (a, b, f', f) = (af'/bf')(bf/af), which is (A', B', B, A) with F, A, B, F' in Déf. 1's order. Rightly not a finding, since the transcription flags it. The printed claims are all proved. '>= 1' in the printed order: IsCrossRatio.one_le. Its hypothesis B' ∈ closedSeg A' B is 'met in this order', and the interior position comes from IsCrossRatio. Existence: exists_isCrossRatio. 'The measure is its logarithm': projMeasure_eq_log. GS-invariance: projMeasure_smul holds for every g : GSE E, hence for GSR n = GSE (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) = GL(n+1, ℝ)/ℝ⁺, the library's GS(n, ℝ). The degenerate values are discussed in readings_ruling: (1a) is the printed formula's ∞, (1b) lies outside the printed domain. The mark does not depend on either. S(n) is generalised to S(E), as disclosed.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p1_mesure_projective_monotone
labels.notes: projMeasure_antitone states both printed assertions with no other hypothesis. (A'', B'') ⊂ (A', B') gives measure(A'', B'' rel AB) <= measure(A', B' rel AB), and AB ⊂ (A1, B1) gives measure rel A1B1 <= measure rel AB. 'Décroît' is weak, as it must be: equality when the segment is unchanged. projMeasure_le_inner and projMeasure_le_outer are stronger: only the new endpoints need to lie on the segment, with no orientation hypothesis. The proof is genuine, not a definitional trick. The inner case writes the points of (A', B') as x a + y b with y/x between 1 and r (exists_coords_of_mem_closedSeg), then uses |log(v/u)| <= |log r| (abs_log_div_le). The outer case writes a and b in coordinates on (A1, B1); the new odds are weighted means of 1 and r (coeff_sums_pos, wavg_mem_uIcc), and the same inequality closes it. No printed proof exists (l.274), and none is needed for a mark. The proof is kernel-checked with standard axioms.

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d2_segment_majore
labels.notes: IsMajoreSeg n k Sg' A' B' reads: IsProjSegment Sg' A' B' ∧ ∃ Sg A B, IsProjSegment Sg A B ∧ Sg' ⊆ Sg ∧ for every compatible φ with Sg ⊆ φ.source, projMeasure (φA) (φA') (φB') (φB) < k. That is l.277-282 word for word, checked against the scan, p. 250. The universal quantifier is never vacuous, because IsProjSegment supplies a chart. isMajoreSeg_iff_exists_chart proves the existential form equivalent, through Ch. 1 Prop. 1 on the connected segment (isPreconnected_seg) and projMeasure_smul. Every compatible chart maps the inner segment into the outer one (image_eq_closedSeg), so the measure is evaluated in the paper's configuration. The definition is non-vacuous: for n >= 1 every segment is majorised by some k (pseudoLength_lt_top, isMajoreSeg_of_chart). Reading (2) is absorbed by the existential over the naming of (A, B). Reading (1b) matters only at n = 0, where the Lean is the literal text (see readings_ruling). The mark stands.

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d3_pseudo_longueur
labels.notes: pseudoLength n Sg M N = ⨅ k : ℝ over IsMajoreSeg n k Sg M N, in EReal, with ⊤ for an empty set. It is >= 0 with no hypothesis (pseudoLength_nonneg) and < ⊤ on every segment for n >= 1 (pseudoLength_lt_top), so it is the paper's real « borne inférieure » wherever that exists. Reading (3) is the paper's own usage (readings_ruling), and the Lean signature matches how 2°, 3°, 5° and 7° use l_V. On the n = 0 consequence: l({m}, m, m) = ⊤ against 1°'s « l_V(M, M) = 0 ». The paper's set of majorants is empty there, so this is the literal value, and it is reported as a finding against the enonce row, not against Déf. 3. See finding 1 for its wording.

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d4_partie_majoree
labels.notes: IsMajorePart n k C = ∀ M ∈ C, ∀ N ∈ C, ∃ Sg ⊆ C, IsMajoreSeg n k Sg M N. That is l.359-363, checked against the scan, p. 251. « Deux points quelconques » is read as including M = N, the usual sense, and this is undisclosed but harmless: for k > 0 and n >= 1 the pairs M = N are automatic (isMajoreSeg_singleton), and the paper only uses k > 0 (Prop. 3, Déf. 5). The witness isMajorePart_singleton (a point, every k > 0, n >= 1) is weak but not definitional, since it builds a real segment through M with cross-ratio 1. Déf. 4 is a definition, so non-vacuity is a sanity check only, and Prop. 3 (T-bz-c2-hilbert) supplies the real witnesses. Downstream note: with this convention Prop. 3 also fails at n = 0, because {M} is not majorised. So T-bz-c2-hilbert inherits finding 1 and should state Prop. 3 under the same ruling.

findings.what: The n = 0 finding is TRUE but overstated, and its witness lies outside the campaign's reading of « variété ». (a) 'Property 1° is false in dimension n = 0' is true of the literal text: in dimension 0 every segment is a point, its only majorising candidate is the same point (A = B), Déf. 1 gives four coincident points no cross-ratio, so no k majorises (M, M) and the « borne inférieure » is that of the empty set. It holds only because the paper leaves the measure of coincident points undefined. Under the natural diagonal convention (cross-ratio (X, X, B, A) = 1, so a point has measure 0 in every configuration), 1° holds for every n, and so does Prop. 3. Going to the author as a bare 'false' would misstate what kind of fact this is. (b) The transcription nowhere states n >= 1: Ch. 1 even names S(0) (« formé de deux points », ch1 l.192), and the library allows n = 0 (Projective/Groups.lean:66). So it is not merely a reading of the chapter's scope. But it is the kind of degenerate case the author has ruled a remark rather than a finding (DEC-120, the disconnected counterexample to Ch. 1 Prop. 1). (c) The Lean witness takes V = S(0), which is two points and DISCONNECTED, whereas CAMPAIGN.md reads « variété » as connected. The same proof works on every V charted on S(0) (audit probe), for instance a point.
findings.fix: Reword the finding and the SCOPE: '1° is not literally true for n = 0: Déf. 1 assigns no measure to coincident points, which in dimension 0 is the only configuration; it holds for n >= 1 (pseudoLength_self), and in every dimension if a point is given measure 0.' Send it with an OQ offering the author three choices: n >= 1 implicit, the point-measure-0 convention, or a finding as printed. Generalise pseudoLength_self_eq_top_dim_zero to any [ChartedSpace (S 0) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid 0)], or add a connected witness, and keep the S(0) case as an instance.

findings.what: The fallback for the master session is misdirected. The degenerate-quadruple convention cannot affect Déf. 1's mark: its printed claims ('>= 1', invariance, 'the log of the cross-ratio') never reach the configurations where the paper's cross-ratio is undefined. Case (1a), A' = A or B' = B alone, is the printed formula's ∞ and binds no label. The one convention with consequences is the coincident-point case (1b). It acts through IsMajoreSeg, so it reaches Déf. 2, Déf. 3 and Déf. 4 alike, and only at n = 0. It also reaches Prop. 3 downstream (T-bz-c2-hilbert): under ⊤, a point of a 0-manifold has no majorised neighbourhood. 'Nothing else changes' is therefore wrong in both directions.
findings.fix: In the notes, replace the fallback with: 'if the author rules the coincident-point case a reading, Déf. 2, 3 and 4 become partial in dimension 0; Déf. 1 and Prop. 1 are unaffected'. Pass the n = 0 point to the T-bz-c2-hilbert and T-bz-c2-proprietes dispatches.

findings.what: The SCOPE and the docstrings say the cross-ratio is infinite when A' = A or B' = B. That fails when the two inner points coincide with the endpoint (A' = B' = A, or A' = B' = B), where the printed formula is 0/0 (undefined), the same status as A = B. The lemmas are correct; only the description lumps together the case that is the printed value (∞) with the case that is a convention (undefined). The latter is exactly what drives finding 1.
findings.fix: Split the SCOPE bullet. '(i) A' = A with B' != A, or B' = B with A' != B: the printed cross-ratio is infinite and the measure is log ∞ = ⊤. (ii) Coincident points (A' = B' ∈ {A, B}, or A = B): the paper defines no cross-ratio and ⊤ is a convention; it matters only in dimension 0 (finding).' Adjust the two docstrings accordingly.
